content.user_title: Build and Debug Browser WebGPU Pipelines
content.value_statement: Browser GPU workloads can fail across devices or lose performance through inefficient resource handling. This skill guides WebGPU implementation with capability checks, usable fallbacks, validation, and targeted measurement.
actual_capabilities: Guide the choice between WebGPU, DOM, Canvas 2D, WebGL2, and Worker or WASM approaches.
Provide asynchronous adapter and device initialization guidance with feature checks, limit checks, and device-loss handling.
Review GPU buffer and texture usage, uploads, alignment requirements, resource reuse, and cleanup.
Guide WGSL validation, pipeline creation, bind-group layout consistency, and scoped error handling.
Explain canvas configuration, resizing, frame scheduling, and queue submission management.
Suggest performance measurements and compatibility tests across representative devices and fallback paths.
limitations: Provides instructions and small TypeScript examples, not a packaged renderer or executable benchmark suite.
WebGPU availability depends on the browser, operating system, GPU, and secure context.
Vercel vgpu library APIs and React Three Fiber scenes are outside this skill's direct workflow.
Experimental HTML-in-Canvas APIs require current compatibility checks and are not presented as production WebGPU primitives.

use_cases.title: Add Reliable Browser GPU Rendering
use_cases.description: Plan initialization, canvas configuration, resource ownership, and usable fallback behavior for a browser rendering feature.

use_cases.title: Review a GPU Compute Workload
use_cases.description: Check compute pipeline structure, storage resources, device limits, and transfer costs before choosing WebGPU over a CPU implementation.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Rendering Performance
use_cases.description: Investigate pipeline churn, repeated allocations, excessive submissions, and readbacks using measurements from representative target devices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Rendering Approach
prompt_templates.prompt: My browser feature is [feature], and target devices are [devices]. Compare WebGPU with simpler options and recommend a compatibility strategy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: decide whether a workload needs WebGPU.

prompt_templates.title: Plan WebGPU Initialization
prompt_templates.prompt: Help initialize WebGPU for [application]. Include capability checks, required features and limits, device-loss handling, and a [fallback renderer] path.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: design reliable adapter and device setup.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pipeline Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [WGSL shader] and [pipeline setup]. Identify interface mismatches, resource usage issues, and validation handling gaps. Explain fixes without assuming optional features.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: debug shaders and pipeline setup.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate GPU Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [render or compute loop] using [CPU timings, GPU timings, and transfer measurements]. Recommend changes and tests against [fallback] on [target devices].
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate measured performance and production readiness.

output_examples.input: Review initialization that assumes every browser returns a usable WebGPU adapter.
output: Check WebGPU availability before requesting an adapter.
Treat a missing adapter or failed device request as a fallback result.
Verify required features and limits before creating the device.
Handle device loss by stopping submissions and rebuilding resources or entering the fallback.

output_examples.input: Suggest a review plan for an animation that recreates pipelines and reads GPU results every frame.
output: Move stable pipeline creation outside the frame loop and reuse buffers, textures, and bind groups.
Measure upload and readback costs separately from CPU frame time and GPU execution.
Remove unnecessary readbacks from the animation loop.
Compare the revised GPU path with its fallback on integrated and discrete GPUs.

output_examples.input: Can I depend on HTML-in-Canvas for a production WebGPU interface?
output_examples.output: Treat the proposed API as experimental and check the current draft. Keep semantic DOM or another renderer as the shipping path.

best_practices: Check required features and limits, then test adapter absence, device loss, and validation failures against a usable fallback.
Reuse stable GPU resources and pipelines, define cleanup explicitly, and keep WGSL independent from untrusted strings.
Benchmark against the fallback on representative devices and separate CPU time, GPU time, transfers, and memory pressure.
anti_patterns: Selecting WebGPU solely for visual effects without checking whether DOM, Canvas 2D, or WebGL meets the workload.
Assuming development GPU capabilities or browser detection guarantees production support.
Recreating pipelines every frame or adding unnecessary GPU-to-CPU readback to the animation loop.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers raw browser WebGPU and WGSL development, including pipelines, resources, validation, device loss, fallbacks, and performance measurement.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does WebGPU work on every target device?
faq.answer: No. Support varies across browsers, operating systems, and GPUs. Check capabilities at runtime and keep a fallback when broad compatibility matters.

faq.question: Does the skill include a complete renderer?
faq.answer: No. It contains guidance and small TypeScript examples. You must integrate and test the implementation in your application.

faq.question: Is WebGPU always faster than WebGL or CPU processing?
faq.answer: No. Small workloads and expensive transfers can remove the benefit. Compare measured performance against the fallback on target devices.

faq.question: Does this skill cover vgpu or React Three Fiber?
faq.answer: No. It directs those workflows to separate skills and focuses on direct browser WebGPU API work.
